policy: The default bootstrap reproduces an exact MediaWiki 1.46 and MinervaNeue snapshot. Every upstream input is obtained from an exact Git commit. Codex styles, design tokens, mixins, and icon-path variables use a separately declared exact version contract. Upstream movement occurs only through an explicit bootstrap refresh or release option. The final stylesheet cascade is generated from Minerva skin options and PHP style-queue declarations rather than a hand-authored upstream CSS import list.

repositories.name: mediawiki-skins-MinervaNeue
repositories.scope: MinervaNeue templates, PHP data contracts, responsive LESS, icons, and interaction behavior sources

repositories.name: mediawiki
repositories.scope: MediaWiki core skinning LESS, ResourceLoader SkinModule and core module registry sources, default variables, and core Codex module CSS sources

repositories.name: mediawiki-extensions-MobileFrontend
repositories.scope: MobileFrontend section transform, collapsible section behavior, and mobile-mode structural reference

repositories.name: design-codex
repositories.scope: Complete locked Codex workspace source used by the upstream build, plus selected generated CSS, token, mixin, icon-path, and SVG vendor outputs

bootstrap.transaction: A refresh or release candidate replaces the lock and manifest only when clone, repository-local upstream builds, staged materialization, generation, and contract checks all succeed. Existing materialized state is retained on failure.
bootstrap.toolingInstall: Root tooling and project-owned upstream build toolchains use npm ci when their lock, runtime, or installation contract fingerprint changes. The lock files are immutable inputs and any attempted mutation fails.
bootstrap.vendorProvenance: Every vendor input comes from an exact Git checkout. Upstream packages that publish generated distributions are rebuilt inside their locked checkout before vendor materialization.

notes: The distributed archive intentionally excludes vendor/, .upstream/, generated CSS/Vue outputs, runtime assets, node_modules/, and upstream build outputs.
The default bootstrap never resolves moving branch heads; it checks out the exact commits recorded above.
--refresh resolves the newest heads of the currently locked release line and is explicit.
--release X.Y resolves RELX_Y explicitly; it does not silently detect or adopt a new stable release.

Default bootstrap reuses fingerprint-matched dependencies and upstream build outputs, stages vendor materialization before atomic replacement, and keeps the last usable state on failure. --clean requests a cold rebuild.

Repositories without upstream build steps use sparse checkout from the declared source inventory. Build-bearing repositories may set sparseCheckout to false so the exact upstream build receives its complete source workspace instead of a guessed file subset.
The design-codex repository is checked out completely at its locked commit, linked to the pinned project-owned build toolchain, and built through its own workspace scripts.
Minerva native skin-theme-clientpref-day/night classes are driven by the thetree theme adapter; no external DarkMode extension is involved.

The final page stylesheet imports are generated from locked Minerva skin options and the conditional style declarations in SkinMinerva.php; css/screen.css does not hand-order upstream ResourceLoader modules.
invariants: The final page stylesheet imports are generated from locked Minerva skin options and SkinMinerva.php conditional style declarations, then serialized using the locked ClientHtml::makeLoad ordering contract.
